headline: Large User Grid Cost Responsibility
short_summary: This bill shifts certain electricity costs, including capacity auction prices and new distribution infrastructure, to high-load energy users like data centers, aiming to reduce residential electricity bills.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Legislators (Sen. Louise Lucas, Del. Destiny LeVere Bolling), Virginia Mercury, environmental and conservation groups.
opponents: Dominion Energy (initially, due to amendments), data centers, large manufacturers.
news_headline: Governor Signs Bills Shifting Data Center Energy Costs
news_summary: Governor Abigail Spanberger signed legislation directing regulators to assign electricity costs to data centers and allowing Dominion Energy to spend more on burying distribution lines. These bills aim to shift capacity market and distribution infrastructure costs to high-load users, potentially saving residential customers money.

headline: Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill requires water users providing water to data centers to report monthly or quarterly water consumption data, including reclaimed water, to the State Water Control Board for enhanced transparency and planning.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Senator Kannan Srinivasan, environmental and conservation groups.
news_headline: Virginia Adds Restrictions, Tracks Data Center Water Use
news_summary: Governor Abigail Spanberger signed bills regulating data centers, including efforts to track their water consumption. This legislation mandates water users to report the total volume of water, including reclaimed water, provided to data centers to the State Water Control Board.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise
short_summary: This bill requires local governments to review potential impacts of large data centers, including mandatory sound assessments and evaluations of impacts on water, agriculture, and historic resources, before approval.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Environmental and conservation groups, neighborhood and parent associations, historic preservation advocates, farmland protection groups, local planning and public health organizations.
opponents: Data center developers, tech industry trade groups, chambers of commerce, commercial real estate associations, pro-growth business or utility groups.
news_headline: Virginia Requires Data Center Siting, Noise Assessments
news_summary: This bill mandates Virginia local governments to review impacts before approving new data centers using 100 megawatts or more. Applicants must submit sound assessments, and localities can request reviews on water, farmland, and historic resources, helping communities make informed decisions.
